b.why:
DECIDABLE in form, with a stated undecidable residue.

The claim is "the progeny of CD56bright are CD56dim" — a precursor-product statement, which the rubric puts on the decidable side. More importantly, its principal rival (Phase A's alternative: a pre-existing CD56dim population is selected/expanded, not converted; and the two-independent-pathway model) is a PURE CLONAL-STRUCTURE statement, and clonal structure is exactly what the primitive returns. "Do the CD56dim cells recovered descend from the CD56bright cells put in, or from a contaminating dim cell?" is answerable with shared-ancestor information and nothing else — it is the one question the barcoding primitive is definitionally competent to settle. Likewise "are CD56bright and CD56dim the same or different lineage" is the rubric's explicit DECIDABLE case, and it has already been posed and answered this way in a primate (Wu 2018, Sci Immunol, PMID 30389798: barcoded macaque HSPC transplant, CD56+CD16- vs CD56-CD16+ NK repertoires "remained distinct under homeostatic conditions over several years").

The load-bearing part of the primitive here is HOW RECENTLY, not merely WHETHER. Every NK cell in one person shares an HSPC ancestor, so bare ancestor-sharing is trivially TRUE under all models. The discriminating readout is whether a bright cell and a dim cell share a recent, post-NK-commitment ancestor (consistent with bright->dim) or only a distant progenitor-level one (two pools branching upstream, the Ding 2024 ENKP/ILCP architecture).

UNDECIDABLE RESIDUE, stated explicitly. Surface NCAM1 density is an activation-modulable variable, so part of this claim is a reversible-state claim, and for that part both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure: a clone spanning both compartments is produced equally by (a) irreversible bright->dim maturation, (b) dim->bright, and (c) cells oscillating between two states. Lineage cannot order a reversible state. It also cannot separate "dim descend from bright" from "bright and dim are clonal siblings branching a few divisions upstream" at the resolution obtainable in a polyclonal human steady state — mtDNA marks label clades, not division events, and PMID 40134031 (Genome Biol 2025) shows mtDNA variants have "limited discriminatory power among different genuine lineages under weak clonal expansion," which is precisely the healthy-adult NK regime. So: the NEGATIVE is decisive (clonally discordant repertoires falsify the arrow), the POSITIVE is confounded on both direction and sibling-vs-parent. Decidable, but one-sidedly.
b.action_if_yes:
IF YES (bright and dim share recent, post-commitment clones; bright-marked clones later appear in dim):

Stated concretely, the next experiment would be to move from "there is a route" to "how fast and driven by what": longitudinal clone-level sampling in the same individual to fit a conversion rate, then a perturbation arm asking which signal drives it (the unreplicated Chan 2007 fibroblast/FGFR1 contact route vs the IL-2/IL-15/IL-12 route that Romagnani 2007 and Chan 2007 disagree about), and a translational arm barcoding a CD56bright-phenotype iPSC/CD34-derived NK product to confirm it matures in the recipient.

Why this branch is weak, written out because B2 turns on it:
(1) It is the default expectation, not a discovery. Shared clonal marks between two mature NK subsets are predicted by essentially every model on the table, including the competing one in which both subsets are fed independently from the same upstream progenitor clones. A YES therefore does not separate the claim from its main rival.
(2) The direction it appears to license is not actually licensed. Establishing bright-before-dim requires ordering within a clone, which reversibility of CD56 density confounds and which mtDNA/integration-site resolution in a polyclonal steady state does not deliver.
(3) The follow-ons are not contingent on the answer. Human in-vivo pulse-chase (the 6,6-D2-glucose sorted-subset design of Patel 2017, PMID 28606987 / PMC5502436, which has never been run on bright vs dim — the only NK deuterium study, PMID 17346281, sorted CD3-CD16+ only and did not resolve the subsets) is the assay that would actually settle direction, and it is a NON-lineage assay one would run instead of, not because of, the clonal experiment. The FGF-vs-cytokine mechanism question and the iPSC-NK maturation question are already being pursued by the field on the assumption that the answer is YES; a YES changes nobody's protocol.
Net: YES confirms the textbook arrow, is non-discriminating against the sibling model, and redirects no downstream work.
b.action_if_no:
IF NO (repertoires clonally discordant; bright-dominant clones stay bright over months-to-years and never seed dim):

This branch is genuinely rich and the next experiments are specific and forced:
(1) It replicates Wu 2018 (PMID 30389798) in the species that matters and kills the stage-4 -> stage-5 arrow of the Freud/Caligiuri five-stage human model, which is the one concrete named dependency Phase A left standing. The immediate follow-on is to look for the human counterpart of the two-pathway ontogeny reported in mouse (Ding 2024, Nat Immunol, PMID 38872000, ENKP vs ILCP): prospectively isolate the candidate human progenitors from bone marrow/tonsil and ask, clonally, which one feeds CD56dim.
(2) It removes the mechanistic explanation for the GATA2-deficiency phenotype (Mace 2013, PMID 23365458: patients maintaining a CD56dim pool with essentially no CD56bright) and makes those patients the natural human genetic test bed rather than an anomaly.
(3) It breaks a manufacturing rationale, which is the sharpest practical consequence. Current iPSC- and CD34-derived NK products come out CD56bright-phenotype and are infused on the assumption that they mature into cytotoxic CD56dim in the patient. Under NO, that assumption is void and the next experiment is defined: determine whether a CD56dim-committed product can be derived directly, and re-read existing infusion trials for whether the transferred bright product ever became dim.
(4) It reclassifies CD56 density as a state/activation variable rather than a developmental stage, which changes how every NK scRNA-seq trajectory paper that orients its pseudotime by this arrow should be read.
b.both_answers_reason:
FALSE on asymmetric payoff. The two branches are not the same experiment, so the claim does not fail the "identical follow-on" test — it fails on the other clause: the YES branch is vacuous in the sense the filter targets.

Laid out against each other: NO overturns a textbook arrow, forces a named search (human ENKP/ILCP-equivalent progenitors), converts GATA2 patients into a test bed, and voids a live cell-manufacturing rationale. YES yields "the consensus model is confirmed" and hands back a set of experiments the field is already running on the assumption that YES is true. Nothing in a lab's plan moves on a YES.

Three specific reasons the YES arm does not survive strict reading:
(a) NON-DISCRIMINATING. Shared clonal marks between two mature NK subsets from one donor are predicted by the claim AND by its principal competitor (both pools fed independently from shared upstream progenitor clones). An outcome both hypotheses predict is not an actionable outcome.
(b) RESOLUTION-LIMITED. Separating parent-child from sibling, and forward from reversible, needs within-clone ordering that the available human clonal marks do not provide in a polyclonal steady state (PMID 40134031). So the YES cannot even be reported as a clean confirmation.
(c) FOLLOW-ON IS NOT CONTINGENT. The experiment that would follow a YES — a human sorted-subset deuterium pulse-chase — is a non-lineage assay that is equally worth running today and is the design that would actually settle direction. If your positive result's next step is "now run the experiment you should have run first," the positive was not load-bearing.

This is a judgement about the decision structure only; the scientific worth of the question is out of scope for this round and I make no claim about it. Note for the shortlist: the sub-question "are CD56bright and CD56dim two separately maintained pools in humans?" — posed as a falsification test rather than as a confirmation of the arrow — would pass B2 much better than the arrow as worded, because its informative arm is the arm that is reachable. If the screen permits reframing, D3 is a candidate for restatement rather than straight elimination.
b.compartments_needed:
Two, and only two, for the core adjudication, both from peripheral blood of the same individual at the same draw:
(A) CD3- CD56bright CD16- NK cells
(B) CD3- CD56dim CD16+ NK cells

Optional compartments that strengthen but are not required:
(C) Bone marrow (aspirate) — to place the branch point relative to progenitors.
(D) Secondary lymphoid tissue where CD56bright is enriched — tonsil (routine tonsillectomy waste) or lymph node (only at surgery).
(E) The clonal-mark substrate, which is the real constraint rather than the tissue: NK cells have no rearranged antigen receptor, so there is no endogenous clone label of the kind the T/B fields get free. The mark must come from (i) somatic mtDNA or nuclear SNVs, (ii) lentiviral integration sites in HSC gene-therapy recipients, (iii) donor/recipient marks after allo-HSCT, or (iv) engineered barcodes, which in a primate means macaque.
b.compartments_obtainable:
YES — and this is the strongest feature of D3. Compartments A and B are obtainable paired from one human, from one routine venipuncture, in any healthy adult, with no procedural gate whatsoever. Not post-mortem. Not surgery-only. Not pregnancy-only. Not mouse-only. Of the compartment pairings in this screen this is close to the least constrained one available.

The gating constraint is the clonal mark, not tissue access, and even that has an existing human substrate: the lentiviral HSC gene-therapy cohort in PMID 39442556 (Nature 2024; 53 patients, MLD/WAS/beta-thalassaemia, integration sites as clonal identity, follow-up to 8 years, PB and BM). I read its Methods (archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/D3_PMC11618100.txt) and confirmed the relevant gap: NK cells were purified as BULK CD56+ by immunomagnetic beads ("CD56 + (CD56 Micro Beads Human, MILTENYI BIOTEC) were isolated in sequence"), with no bright/dim split anywhere in the study. So the human clonal substrate for this exact question exists and has already been banked longitudinally; what is missing is a FACS sort of bright vs dim in place of a bulk CD56 bead pull. Analogous human substrates: allo-HSCT genome-wide somatic-mutation clonal tracking (PMID 39478227).

Optional compartments: (C) bone marrow needs an aspirate — a real but routine procedural gate in transplant/GT cohorts where marrow is already drawn; (D) tonsil is available as routine surgical waste, lymph node only at surgery. Neither is required for the core bright-vs-dim adjudication.
b.compartment_notes:
SPECIES: this is a human-only claim, and the direction of the constraint is the opposite of most rows in this screen — it is not mouse-only, it CANNOT be posed in mouse. Mouse NK cells do not carry the CD56bright/CD56dim partition (NCAM1 is not a mouse NK subset marker; mouse maturation is staged on CD27/CD11b, which is claim D2). The available animal proxy is rhesus macaque, and even there the axis is not identical: macaque subsets are CD56+CD16- vs CD56-CD16+, whereas human CD56dim are CD56+CD16+. Wu 2018 (PMID 30389798) therefore answered an analogous, not the same, question — which is exactly why the human version remains open despite a clonal-grade primate result already existing.

PURITY IS THE CRUX, AND CLONAL MARKING IS WHAT FIXES IT: CD56dim are ~90% of blood NK, so a 1-2% dim carry-over into a sorted bright fraction is, in absolute terms, a large dim population — the failure mode Phase A flagged for the Chan 2007 NOD-SCID arm. This is precisely the artefact that per-cell clonal marks neutralise, since a carry-over dim cell carries a mark and a converted one carries its parent's. Design implication: index/single-cell sorting with per-cell marks, not bulk repertoire comparison of two sorted pools.

YIELD: from a standard 50 mL draw expect ~5x10^6 NK, of which bright is ~5-10%, so ~2-5x10^5 bright cells — adequate for mtscATAC/MAESTER. For integration-site PCR at the depth used in PMID 39442556 (12 mL draws), the bright fraction is likely yield-limited and would want leukapheresis or pooled timepoints; worth costing before committing.

SETTING SELECTION MATTERS MORE THAN TISSUE ACCESS: PMID 40134031 shows mtDNA marks discriminate lineages well only under stringent clonal expansion. Healthy-adult polyclonal NK is the weak-expansion regime where they do not. If this claim is pursued, the compartments should be drawn from a stringent-expansion setting — gene-therapy or allo-HSCT recipients, aged donors with clonal haematopoiesis, or HCMV+ donors carrying large adaptive NKG2C+ clones — rather than from a young healthy donor, where the compartments are trivially obtainable but the marks will not resolve.

b.why:
TRUE, with one scope condition and one design condition, both stated below.

FORM. The claim is "the progeny of A are B" (A = conventional NKG2C-/FcRg+ NK; B = adaptive NK), not "A becomes functionally B-like". It is therefore in the decidable class — PROVIDED compartment B is operationalised as a SORT GATE (NKG2C+, and per Liu 2016 PMID 27117418 the NKG2C-independent adaptive gate: FcRg-/SYK-/CD57+/LILRB1+, demethylated IFNG CNS1) rather than as a function ("memory", "recall"). If B were defined by recall capacity, lineage could not decide it. Note the naming problem this exposes: NKG2C is dispensable (11/44 KLRC2-/- HCMV+ donors have bona fide adaptive expansions), so a barcoding study gated only on NKG2C would decide a narrower claim than the one the field actually holds. The gate must be the adaptive signature, not the receptor.

WHY THE PRIMITIVE IS NOT TRIVIALLY SATISFIED. All NK cells in one person share an HSPC ancestor, so "do A and B share an ancestor?" is trivially YES and carries no information. The claim is decidable only through the RECENCY half of the primitive — which is exactly what the primitive supplies. The three live models make non-overlapping predictions about MRCA depth: (i) CONVERSION — an expanded adaptive clone's MRCA with a contemporaneous conventional NKG2C- cell sits at mature-NK depth, so one recent, NK-private clonotype contains both conventional and adaptive cells; (ii) SELECTION of a pre-existing already-NKG2C+ founder (Ruckert 2022's own stated model; Bjorkstrom 2011 PMC3023129; Adams 2019) — the adaptive clone's recent relatives are all already adaptive, and the MRCA with conventional NK sits only at progenitor depth; (iii) SEPARATE PROGENITOR (Bozzano 2021; Sci Adv 2025 thymic; cILC1 route PMID 42054258) — no sharing with the conventional NK pool even at NKP depth. Three distinguishable depth signatures; the tool is doing real work, not confirming a tautology.

RECENCY CALIBRATION IS THE CRUX AND IS AVAILABLE. A shared mtDNA variant is informative only if progenitor-level origin can be excluded — Ruckert 2022 warns of precisely this ("mitochondrial mutations of conventional NK cells ... might instead be present already on the progenitor level"). The control is co-profiling autologous T/B/monocytes from the same draw: a variant also carried by unrelated lineages is progenitor-level; a variant private to NK and confined to a tight clone is recent. Feasibility precedent exists: PMID 42242233 (Cancer Cell 2026) reconstructs cross-compartment mtDNA clonal relationships across 218,715 cells from matched tumour/tissue/blood; PMID 38253266 (Nature 2024) does deep mtDNA detection with joint state readout.

NOT A REVERSIBLE-STATE CLAIM (checked explicitly). The reversible-state exclusion does not fire here. The adaptive endpoint is a stably heritable epigenetic configuration (IFNG CNS1 demethylation, FCER1G/SYK/ZBTB16 silencing) that Ruckert 2022 shows persisting within the SAME mtDNA clonotypes over 7, 11 and 19 months; and Bjorkstrom 2011 reports the authors tested and could not induce NKG2C on NKG2C- cells. So it is not an oscillating state where both answers yield the same clonal structure.

DESIGN CONDITION (the honest limit). The barcode alone locates the branch point but does not ORIENT it: a recent clonotype containing both conventional and adaptive cells is equally consistent with A->B, B->A, and a bifurcating common parent. Direction requires the longitudinal form of the same primitive — which clonotype carried which phenotype at t1 versus t2. A single cross-sectional timepoint decides branch DEPTH only; the directional arrow needs repeat sampling across the infection/expansion. Decidable, but only in the longitudinal design.
b.action_if_yes:
YES = adaptive clones share recent, NK-private MRCAs with contemporaneous conventional NKG2C-/FcRg+ cells, and at the pre-expansion baseline the founder variant is carried by a phenotypically conventional cell.

VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: identify WHICH conventional NK cell is licensed to convert — a question the YES result poses and does not answer. Use the mtDNA clonotype as an index back into the baseline sample already in hand and read out the pre-conversion cell's own chromatin/surface state: CD56bright vs CD56dim, NKG2A+ vs KIR+, whether it is the CXXC5+ immature precursor nominated by PMC11686228 (Front Immunol 2024, which places an adaptive-NK precursor present at equal frequency in CMV+ and CMV- people), and critically whether KLRC2-locus accessibility or IFNG CNS1 demethylation is ALREADY partially present before infection (i.e. whether "conventional" founders are in fact pre-primed).

Then convert descriptive to prospective: from an HCMV-seronegative donor, FACS-sort the nominated precursor gate versus its complement, and challenge in the autologous HCMV-infected fibroblast/monocyte coculture system (Guma 2006 / Rolle 2014 PMC4348979) or a humanised-mouse HCMV model, scoring adaptive output by the NKG2C-INDEPENDENT signature so the readout does not depend on the receptor Liu 2016 showed to be dispensable. This is the sort-the-precursor experiment nobody has run: Phase A records that no study anywhere purified an NKG2C-depleted conventional population and followed it for acquisition of the adaptive phenotype.

TRANSLATIONAL CONSEQUENCE (different from the NO branch): conversion being real makes "adaptive" a MANUFACTURABLE STATE rather than a donor property. ADAPT-NK (Blood Adv 2022, PMC9628692) currently screens CMV-seropositive "superdonors" for large pre-existing adaptive subpopulations; under YES that screening step is an inefficiency to be engineered away, and the induction protocol — which conventional subset plus which signal — becomes the defined development target.
b.action_if_no:
NO = adaptive clones' recent relatives are exclusively adaptive/NKG2C+; the MRCA with conventional NK appears only at progenitor depth (variant also present in autologous T/B/monocyte lineages); the pre-expansion baseline already carries the founder variant in an NKG2C+/adaptive-primed cell.

VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT — and it is not the YES experiment, because NO leaves TWO sub-hypotheses standing that this dataset cannot separate: (a) the founder is a mature but already-adaptive-primed cell inside the conventional NK developmental stream, versus (b) the founder descends from a SEPARATE progenitor branch. Separating them requires acquiring a compartment the YES branch never needs: bone marrow aspirate (CD34+ HSPC, CLP, NKP, stage 3-4 NK precursors) plus the circulating Lin-CD34+DNAM-1bright CXCR4+ precursor of Bozzano 2021 (PMID 33493558) and circulating ILC1s (PMID 42054258), from the same individual, asking whether the adaptive founder clonotype maps to a progenitor branch distinct from the one feeding conventional NK. A positive result there promotes Bozzano 2021 / the Sci Adv 2025 thymic progenitor (PMID 40779632) from "alternative explanation" to "the actual origin".

SECOND, PROSPECTIVE AND QUANTITATIVE: if the founder pool pre-exists, its SIZE and CLONAL DIVERSITY before infection should predict the magnitude and clonal composition of the post-infection expansion. Testable in a D+/R- transplant cohort with banked baseline draws, and it already has a human precedent to confirm or refute — Bjorkstrom 2011 (PMC3023129) found CMV-IgG-negative hantavirus patients had low baseline NKG2C+ numbers and never expanded despite identical acute viral insult. That is a pre-registered, falsifiable prediction, not a conclusion.

TRANSLATIONAL CONSEQUENCE (opposite to YES): the problem stops being induction and becomes repertoire selection. Superdonor screening is then the correct irreducible design rather than a workaround, and the target shifts to identifying and sorting the founder pool in seronegative donors. Separately, the diagnostic use of NKG2C to call clonally restricted NK populations non-neoplastic (Mod Pathol 2026, PMID 41786213) rests on adaptive NK being a normal expansion of the conventional NK lineage and would need restating if the origin is a distinct progenitor.
b.both_answers_reason:
TRUE — the two branches are not the same experiment, and neither is vacuous. Tested against the three failure modes:

(1) SAME EXPERIMENT? No. YES stays in peripheral blood, looks BACKWARD into data already collected (index the clonotype into the archived baseline to profile the pre-conversion cell), then forward to an induction protocol. NO forces acquisition of a compartment YES never needs — bone marrow / progenitors — plus a prospective pool-size predictor in a transplant cohort. Different tissue, different assay, different analysis.

(2) ONE BRANCH VACUOUS? No. The YES branch is not "conversion is real, done": YES establishes THAT conversion happens and leaves entirely open WHICH conventional cell converts, which is the question with the manufacturing payoff. The NO branch is not "selection, as expected, move on": NO leaves two live sub-hypotheses (already-primed mature founder vs separate progenitor branch) that the same primitive can separate one level deeper in the tree, and it hands over a falsifiable quantitative prediction (baseline pool size/diversity gates expansion magnitude) with an existing human observation to test it against.

(3) DIVERGENT DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE? Yes, and they are opposite in direction: YES makes adaptive NK an inducible state and makes superdonor screening obsolete; NO makes it a selectable pre-existing repertoire, makes superdonor screening correct and irreducible, and puts a live question mark over the NKG2C-based benign/neoplastic diagnostic call.

ONE HONEST CAVEAT, recorded rather than suppressed: a third outcome is possible — MRCA depth unresolvable, i.e. shared variants that cannot be assigned to progenitor versus recent origin. Ruckert 2022 flags exactly this for the conventional NK compartment. That outcome is neither YES nor NO; it is a coverage/depth failure and is what the Phase C power thresholds (chrM coverage, informative-variant count, cells per donor per compartment) exist to catch in advance. It does not make either branch vacuous, but it is the most likely way this claim dies at Phase C rather than at Phase B.
b.compartments_needed:
CORE (all four required for the primary readout):
1. Peripheral blood CONVENTIONAL NK — CD3-CD14-CD19-CD56+ NKG2C- FcRg+ sort gate.
2. Peripheral blood ADAPTIVE NK — NKG2C+ AND, per Liu 2016, the NKG2C-independent adaptive gate (FcRg-/SYK-/CD57+/LILRB1+). Gating on NKG2C alone decides a narrower claim than the field holds.
3. Autologous NON-NK leukocytes from the SAME draw (T, B, monocytes). Not optional garnish — this is the progenitor-depth calibrator. Without it a shared mtDNA variant cannot be assigned to "recent conversion" versus "inherited from a common HSPC", and the whole readout is uninterpretable (Ruckert 2022's own stated caveat).
4. A PRE-EXPANSION TIMEPOINT from the SAME individual (baseline PBMC before primary HCMV infection or before reactivation). Required for the DIRECTIONAL claim only; the branch-depth version can be run cross-sectionally.

ADDITIONAL, ONLY IF THE ANSWER IS NO:
5. Bone marrow CD34+ HSPC / CLP / NKP / stage 3-4 NK precursors.
6. Circulating Lin-CD34+DNAM-1bright CXCR4+ precursors (Bozzano 2021) and circulating ILC1 (PMID 42054258) — both blood, so free.
7. Thymus (only to test the Sci Adv 2025 thymic-progenitor origin).
8. Secondary lymphoid organ NK (only to test the Blood 2025 "transitional precursor in SLO" model).
b.compartments_obtainable:
YES for the core, and this is the unusual case in this screen where the two compartments are both in blood.

Items 1-3 are three FACS gates on a SINGLE peripheral blood draw from one living human. No surgery, no post-mortem, no pregnancy, no mouse. Precedent that the paired sort plus mtDNA readout actually works on exactly these cells: Ruckert 2022 (PMC9663309) sorted NKG2C+ and NKG2C- NK 1:1 from the same donors and ran mtscATAC/ASAP-seq; PMID 42242233 (Cancer Cell 2026) resolved cross-compartment mtDNA clonal relationships across 218,715 cells from matched tumour, tissue and blood in the same patients; PMID 39236287 tracked mtDNA-marked populations at 0.1-1% frequency in post-HSCT clinical samples.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT ACTUALLY BITES IS TIME, NOT TISSUE. Item 4 — the pre-expansion baseline — cannot be obtained opportunistically, because primary HCMV infection is unpredictable in healthy adults. It exists only where a baseline draw is banked by protocol: (a) D+/R- solid-organ transplant recipients (Lopez-Verges 2011's own design); (b) allo-HSCT/UCBT recipients with cryopreserved pre-transplant PBMC (precedent: PMC11686228, an MSKCC cohort of 267 HCT patients with protocolised weekly CMV monitoring from D14); (c) congenital/infant primary-infection cohorts. Of these, D+/R- SOT is the CLEAN one: in allo-HSCT the reconstituting NK cells arise de novo from grafted HSPC rather than from mature conventional NK, so the "A" being followed is a progenitor, not a conventional NK cell, and the arrow being tested silently changes. Lymphodepletion and immunosuppression are confounds in both.

Item 5 (bone marrow) requires an aspirate — invasive but routine, obtainable from the same living human, easiest in patients already undergoing marrow sampling or in HSCT donors. Item 6 is free (blood). Item 7 THYMUS IS SURGICAL-ONLY (paediatric cardiac surgery) and in practice cannot be paired with an adult blood adaptive compartment from the same individual. Item 8 SLO NK is SURGICAL OR POST-MORTEM/deceased-donor only. None of 7-8 is needed for the primary readout; both sit behind the NO branch.

UNVERIFIED FEASIBILITY ASSUMPTION, flagged rather than assumed: every banked baseline is cryopreserved, and mtscATAC-seq is a fixed-cell, intact-mitochondria protocol. The Nat Protoc method paper (PMID 36792778) covers primary haematopoietic cells and several cell-processing/flow workflows, but I did not confirm a validated cryopreserved-PBMC arm. Cryo-compatibility of the baseline samples must be verified at Phase C, not presumed.
b.compartment_notes:
MOUSE_ONLY = FALSE, on three independent grounds. (i) The claim text itself scopes this as HUMAN and explicitly excludes the Ly49H/MCMV homolog as a different transition. (ii) The mouse homolog has ALREADY been single-cell fate-mapped — Grassmann 2019 (PMID 31103380) and Flommersfeld 2021 (PMID 34437840, PMC8528403) transferred single retrogenic colour-barcoded Ly49H+ NK cells and read out clonal progeny — so a mouse run would re-occupy answered ground while answering a transition the claim disowns. (iii) Prereg 4.3: mtDNA barcoding is weak in young inbred mice, so the endogenous-barcode route is specifically a human strength here.

MACAQUE, considered and set aside. Truitt/Dunbar 2019 (PMID 31649681, PMC6794559) and PMC9808525 (2022, barcoded tissue NK across compartments) provide true lentiviral barcoding plus paired tissue compartments, but three things disqualify them for this arrow: the barcode tags the HSPC, so shared barcodes between conventional and adaptive NK prove common HSPC ancestry — the trivially-true answer, not mature-cell conversion; tissue compartments require necropsy; and RhCMV is not HCMV.

DEFINITIONAL NOTE THAT PROPAGATES INTO COMPARTMENT DESIGN: because NKG2C is dispensable (Liu 2016; Della Chiesa 2014; Goodier 2014), sorting compartment B on NKG2C alone would systematically miss the KLRC2-independent adaptive cells and could manufacture a spurious NO. The B gate must be the adaptive epigenetic/surface signature with NKG2C as one marker among several.

SAMPLE-ECONOMY NOTE: compartments 1, 2, 3 and 6 all come from one tube of blood, so the marginal cost of the NO-branch blood precursors is zero and they should be collected in the primary draw regardless of the expected answer — this is the one design choice that keeps both B2 branches live off a single collection.

b.why:
This is the rubric's second bullet ("A becomes functionally B-like") in its purest form, compounded by the fourth (reversible/graded state within one lineage). Four independent reasons, in order of force.

(1) B HAS NO LINEAGE-INDEPENDENT DEFINITION. "CIML NK" is scored by one thing only: enhanced IFN-gamma on restimulation. Cooper 2009 (PMC2644138) shows the cells are phenotypically indistinguishable from IL-15-only controls across CD69, CD11b, CD11c, gp49B, B220, CD122, IL-15Ralpha, IL-12Rbeta1 and CD127, are granzyme-B NEGATIVE, and kill YAC-1 no better ("all 4 groups of NK cells exhibited similar cytotoxicity"). So B is co-extensive with the assay used to define it. The barcoding primitive returns ancestry, not function; something else must still call a cell "B", and once the recall assay has called it, the barcode has added nothing to the claim's arrow.

(2) THE CONVERSION STEP INVOLVES NO CELL DIVISION, SO IT WRITES NOTHING INTO THE GENEALOGY. The protocol is 13-16 h. Cooper 2009 Fig 4 is explicit that generation-0 (never-divided) preactivated cells make as much IFN-gamma as generations 1-3. Lineage structure is created by division. A transformation that occurs without division leaves the clonal tree of the population IDENTICAL before and after — under the conversion model AND under the selection model. "Do these two cells share an ancestor, and how recently" returns the same answer either way. There is no lineage signal to read because none was generated.

(3) A AND B ARE UNCONTESTEDLY THE SAME LINEAGE. Nobody in this literature proposes that CIML NK cells are non-NK-derived; Keppel 2013 already excluded de novo endogenous NK development with Rag2-/-gc-/- hosts. The only lineage question with a live disagreement — donor vs host — is a two-population question already settled by CD45.1/CD45.2 congenics in mouse, which needs no clonal resolution at all.

(4) THE REAL DISPUTE (SELECTION vs CONVERSION) IS NOT A CLONAL QUESTION. The hypothesized pre-existing responsive compartment is a DIFFERENTIATION STAGE — CD56bright/NKG2A+/CD57-/KIR- in Romee 2012's own marker correlations, CD27hi in mouse — not a clone. Its members are distributed across clonotypes. So "selection of that subset" and "conversion of everything" both predict a broad, essentially unbiased clonotype draw. Both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure, which is exactly the rubric's disqualifying condition. Add that the state is reversible and dose/duration-graded (5 h gives a weaker effect than overnight; Keppel 2013 concedes in print it "could represent a residual priming effect, rather than a memory-like response"), so "converted then decayed" and "never converted" are also clonally identical.

STRONGEST COUNTER-CONSIDERATION, AND WHY IT DOES NOT RESCUE DECIDABILITY. There is one genuinely lineage-shaped design: barcode a proliferating NK pool, split sibling cells into preactivation vs control, and ask whether recall competence is concordant within a barcode (clone-intrinsic, i.e. pre-existing) or uncorrelated (induced). That is the primitive used correctly. But it requires clones with multiple members, which requires 10-14 days of feeder/IL-2 expansion at 300-450 fold to manufacture — precisely what Allan/Dunbar 2023 (PMID 36699615, PMC9842935) did in barcoded rhesus macaques, finding correlated clone-intrinsic proliferative behaviour across two feeder conditions (Pearson r 0.52-0.67). (1) A HARD, ACCESS-INDEPENDENT CONSTRAINT. The assay that DEFINES compartment B — restimulation followed by intracellular IFN-gamma staining — is destructive. The one pairing that would settle the claim, the same individual cell before and after preactivation, is therefore physically impossible no matter how good the tissue access is. The only workaround is a live IFN-gamma secretion-capture sort, which itself perturbs the cell. No amount of compartment availability fixes this.

(2) THE COMPARTMENTS ARE NOT SEPARATED, WHICH IS THE PROBLEM, NOT A CONVENIENCE. Lineage adjudication earns its keep when A and B sit in different places and you ask whether one seeded the other. Here A and B are the same cells in the same dish 16 hours apart. There is no spatial or temporal gap for ancestry to bridge.

(3) COMPARTMENT B IS OBTAINABLE BUT NOT IDENTIFIABLE IN THE SETTING THAT CARRIES THE CLINICAL WEIGHT. Post-HCT, the reconstituting NK compartment is HLA-matched to the infused ML product, so the anti-HLA mAb readout used in Romee 2016 fails (Berrien-Elliott 2022, PMID 35196021; Bednarski 2022, PMID 34871371, which identifies "persisting ML NK cells" purely by viSNE clustering on CD56-hi/NKG2A/CD62L). NK cells carry no rearranged receptor, so clonal tracking needs either transduction (which needs proliferation) or mtDNA heteroplasmy (which marks HSC-level families fixed decades earlier and is therefore uninformative about a 16 h state change). Generating clones with members to compare requires the 10-14 day feeder/IL-2 expansion of Allan/Dunbar 2023 — replacing the claim's no-division protocol with a fortnight of driven proliferation. The claim as stated is only testable by lineage after you have stopped testing the claim as stated.

b.why:
FALSE on four independent grounds, any one of which is sufficient.

(1) WRONG PREDICATE. The claim's predicate is a function — % specific 51Cr release on 721.221/K562, % conjugates with polarized MTOC and perforin at 20 min, CD107a exposure. The primitive returns shared-ancestry and nothing else. This is verbatim the "A becomes functionally B-like" form that prereg 3 fixes as not decidable. Phase A already recorded is_lineage_claim=FALSE: no clone, barcode, congenic marker, transfer, fate map or recorder appears anywhere in Kopcow 2005, Verma 2000, Tokmadzic 2002, El Costa 2008 or Siewiera 2013.

(2) THE ANSWER IS FIXED BY CONSTRUCTION, SO IT CANNOT COVARY WITH THE CLAIM. The two things compared are one bead-purified dNK population at t=0 and the same dish at 36 h. They are trivially co-lineal — one prep, one tube. The primitive's output is known before the experiment is run, so it carries zero information about whether the claim is true. A test whose result is determined by the sampling scheme rather than by the hypothesis is not a test.

(3) REVERSIBLE STATE WITHIN ONE LINEAGE — the decisive point. Cytotoxic competence here is an environmentally-set, reversible functional state, and Kopcow's own Discussion says so verbatim: "the immunosuppressive environment of the decidua might be responsible for blocking MTOC and granule polarization. Regain of cytotoxicity may result from the removal of dNK from this environment." At least three mutually exclusive readings — (a) IL-15 induces the state, (b) leaving the decidua de-represses it, (c) it was never absent (El Costa 2008 PMID 18713971: fresh uncultured dNK lyse after NKp46 crosslinking; Siewiera 2013 PMID 23592985: fresh dNK kill autologous HCMV-infected decidual fibroblasts) — all produce the IDENTICAL clonal structure. Every truth-value of the claim maps to the same barcode distribution, so the barcode distribution cannot discriminate among them. That is the definition of not decidable.

(4) OPERATIONAL DEGENERACY. Over the 12-36 h window purified dNK essentially do not divide, so no two cells acquire a shared recent ancestor during the experiment; the primitive collapses to per-cell tagging and returns "no shared ancestor" for every pair whether or not the claim holds. Extending culture until clones do arise substitutes a different experiment, since long culture is itself the confound being adjudicated. Compounding this, barcoding primary human NK requires activating transduction culture (cf. barcoded lentiviral NK delivery, PMID 40621477), which imposes the exact ex vivo perturbation at issue — the instrument creates the artefact it is meant to measure.

The one sub-question lineage could in principle touch — selection of a pre-existing competent minority versus conversion of each cell — is NOT the claim as written, and would additionally require functionally phenotyping the ancestor, which the chromium-release assay consumes.

b.why:
DECIDABLE, but only in the same-lineage/different-lineage form, and only with the label applied downstream of the NK progenitor.

WHY TRUE. The falsifiable content Phase A itself names — conversion vs "two independent lineages" — is exactly an MRCA-depth question, which is what the primitive returns. Under two independent lineages, mature blood cNK and liver/skin trNK coalesce only at or above the common progenitor: every cross-compartment cell pair has a deep MRCA, while within-compartment pairs can be shallow. Under conversion, individual clones straddle the two compartments with shallow, post-progenitor MRCAs. That asymmetry in the cross- vs within-compartment coalescent-depth distribution is a direct readout of "do they share an ancestor and how recently," so the claim's load-bearing alternative is adjudicable.

WHAT IS NOT DECIDABLE, AND MUST BE SCOPED OUT.
(1) Direction. A clone found in both compartments is equally consistent with cNK -> trNK, with trNK export back to blood, and with a shared recent precursor that seeded both in parallel. The arrow in "cNK -> trNK" is NOT recovered by clonal structure alone; it needs a timestamp (label the mature cNK pool only, after the trNK pool already exists) so that appearance of label in trNK is directional by construction.
(2) The parenthetical, "acquisition of a residency phenotype," read literally as a phenotype/state statement, is NOT decidable — lineage does not measure whether residency was acquired, only whether the cells are clonally continuous.
(3) The reversible-state trap partially bites. If residency is reversible (an ex-trNK can re-enter circulation, as documented for ex-TRM in the T-cell field), shared clones cannot separate one-way conversion from a single interconverting pool — both give clones spanning both compartments. Crucially, though, the reversibility ambiguity sits INSIDE the "one lineage" branch; it does not collapse the one-lineage vs two-lineage discrimination, which is why this is TRUE rather than FALSE.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT THAT FALLS OUT OF THE PRIMITIVE. HSC/HSPC-level barcoding cannot decide this claim: both hypotheses predict shared HSPC barcodes across compartments, because both candidate lineages descend from the same HSCs. This is exactly the ceiling on Wu 2022 (PMID 36605190 / PMC9808525, barcoded autologous HSPC transplant in rhesus, blood vs liver/spleen/lung/GI NK) — they observe both PB-shared and tissue-private NK clones, but at HSPC-clone resolution "shared" does not separate "a cNK converted" from "one HSPC clone independently fed two lineages." The decidable design needs either an inducible label at or below the mature cNK stage (Ncr1-CreERT2 x barcode/Confetti, induced after the resident pool is established) or enough sub-clonal resolution (mtDNA sub-clone structure via mtscATAC-seq/MAESTER, rooted on same-donor HSPCs) to measure coalescent DEPTH rather than mere set overlap.
b.action_if_yes:
YES = clones straddle mature circulating cNK and tissue trNK with shallow (post-progenitor) MRCA; the trNK pool is clonally continuous with the mature circulating pool.

Very next experiment: the conversion flux is now a measurable quantity, so perturb the source and re-read the SAME clonal output. Concretely — Ncr1-CreERT2 driving both the inducible barcode/Confetti and Tgfbr2-flox (TGF-betaRII is the named requirement in the sibling uterine claim, Barahona/Yokoyama), tamoxifen after the resident pool is established, then score whether cNK-derived barcodes still enter the liver/skin trNK compartment and at what rate. Paired arm: naive vs locally infected tissue (VACV/HSV ear skin, per the Gasteiger-lab design, PMID 38157853) to test whether entry is a steady-state trickle or inflammation-gated — which is the specific thing Sojka parabiosis could not see, since parabiosis tests pool replenishment at steady state, not inducible entry.

This is a new mouse, a new perturbation, and a new statistic (barcode entry rate under a genetic block). It is motivated ONLY by YES: with NO there is no source to knock out.
b.action_if_no:
NO = cross-compartment MRCAs are uniformly deep; trNK clones are tissue-private and coalesce with blood cNK only at or above the progenitor.

Very next experiment: the question flips from "how much flux" to "which progenitor, and when," which is a different sampling program, not a conclusion. Concretely — move the labeling window earlier and swap in the candidate source compartments: pulse-label in the fetal/perinatal window, and compare an ILC-progenitor-restricted CreER (Il7r/Rag1/PLZF-class) against Ncr1-CreER, asking which progenitor compartment shares a SHALLOW MRCA with adult liver trNK. In parallel, use the within-tissue clone-size distribution to test whether the resident pool is self-maintained by local proliferation rather than fed from outside at all. In the human arm this means dropping blood cNK as the comparator and adding fetal liver / BM ILC progenitors / adult BM CD34+ to the panel.

Precedent that this branch is productive rather than terminal: the tissue-macrophage field's NO answer (tissue macrophages are not monocyte-derived) is what launched the fetal-origin program. Same structural shape here.

TRUE, and I tried to break it.

The two branches do not collapse. YES points at a KNOWN source and asks a mechanism/requirement question — build Ncr1-CreERT2 x barcode x Tgfbr2-flox, measure blocked entry rate. NO points at an UNKNOWN source and asks an ontogeny question — shift the labeling window to the fetal/perinatal period, swap the comparator compartments to progenitors, and test in-situ self-renewal via clone-size distribution. Different mouse, different compartments sampled, different summary statistic. Neither is "we would conclude X and move on."

Honest deductions, recorded rather than hidden:
(1) SHARED CONTROL, NOT SHARED EXPERIMENT. Both branches need same-individual HSPCs to root the tree and set the baseline coalescent depth. Under YES that sample is a control; under NO it becomes the primary search space and gets extended backward in developmental time. The overlap is a control, not the experiment, so it does not trip the "same thing" rule.
(2) THE LIKELY REAL ANSWER IS MIXED, NOT BINARY. Wu 2022 (PMID 36605190) already sees both PB-shared and tissue-private NK clones in macaque; mouse skin shows infection-driven conversion (PMID 38157853) while liver parabiosis (Sojka 2014) shows no steady-state exchange. So the expected result is "some fraction, under some condition." This is the main thing that could make the experiment descriptive rather than decisive. It does NOT flip the verdict, because a mixture makes the FRACTION the object of study and both branch experiments then apply to their respective fractions — but it does mean the claim should be preregistered with a quantitative threshold (what cNK-derived fraction of the trNK pool counts as YES) rather than as a binary, or it will resolve to an uninformative "both."
(3) The directional version of this experiment carries the actionability. If only the non-directional human mtDNA version is run, YES degrades toward "they are one lineage" — still not vacuous, since it kills the two-independent-lineage alternative Phase A flags, but the YES-branch follow-up above requires the mouse timestamp to be well-posed.
b.compartments_needed:
THREE compartments, needed simultaneously from one individual:

A. Circulating conventional NK — peripheral blood (human venipuncture; mouse blood + spleen). Trivial.

B. Tissue-resident NK from ONE defined tissue. The claim must name the tissue, because feasibility differs sharply:
   - LIVER (the compartment Sojka 2014 parabiosis actually addresses): human via deceased-donor liver perfusate, or via surgical resection (hepatectomy/metastasectomy), both with paired blood from the same individual.
   - SKIN: punch biopsy + paired blood, outpatient and repeatable — but trNK are rare in normal human skin, so cell-number limiting.
   - UTERUS/ENDOMETRIUM: pipelle biopsy + paired blood, outpatient, repeatable, non-pregnant; uNK are abundant, which is the best cell-number profile of the options. Decidua proper is pregnancy-only (termination/delivery).
   - LUNG/GUT: resection or endoscopic biopsy + paired blood.

C. A ROOTING compartment: HSPC/progenitors (BM aspirate or mobilised CD34+) from the SAME individual. This is not optional. Without it you cannot convert "clone shared vs private" into "MRCA shallow vs deep," and the whole discrimination in B1 collapses — you cannot distinguish a shared HSPC clone from a genuine peripheral conversion.
b.compartments_obtainable:
TRUE, with a cell-number caveat that is the real bottleneck.

Paired A+B from one living human is routine: blood + endometrial pipelle (outpatient), blood + skin punch, blood + liver resection at surgery. None of the required compartments is post-mortem-only, pregnancy-only, or mouse-only. Adding C from a living donor costs one extra invasive procedure (BM aspirate). All three come paired and unforced from a single deceased organ donor (vertebral-body BM + blood + multiple solid organs), which is the standard organ-donor tissue pipeline.

Verified precedent that in-life paired sampling works in a primate: Wu 2022 (PMID 36605190) took liver and spleen by laparoscopy, gut by endoscopic pinch biopsy, and LN by surgical excision, serially, from LIVING barcoded macaques alongside blood.

THE CAVEAT, from the same paper: subset-resolved sorting of tissue NK (CD56/CD16 subsets out of each organ) was only possible in the ONE animal that came to autopsy — the serial in-life biopsies gave paired tissue+blood but not enough cells to sort resident NK subsets. So paired sampling is obtainable; paired sampling at the DEPTH needed for clonal statistics on a rare resident subset pushes you toward organ-donor, autopsy, or surgical-resection-scale material rather than needle biopsy. This is the practical constraint that should be preregistered, and it argues for endometrium (abundant uNK, repeatable outpatient sampling) or resection-scale liver over skin.

SPLIT FEASIBILITY — the two versions of this experiment have different species ceilings, and this should be recorded explicitly:

- The DIRECTIONAL version (does a mature cNK become a trNK) is MOUSE-ONLY, because it requires an inducible label restricted to the mature cNK pool (Ncr1-CreERT2 x barcode/Confetti, induced after the resident pool exists). No human equivalent.

- G4 note: the structurally identical question (are tissue-resident cells clonally continuous with the circulating pool, or a separate lineage?) has already been worked over in the T-cell field via TCR-based clonal overlap between TRM and circulating memory, and in the myeloid field via fetal-origin fate mapping, where the NO answer was the productive one. Occupancy in those fields should be checked before this is shortlisted.

b.why: The fork T3 actually turns on is invisible to a shared-ancestor primitive. Three reasons, in order of force. (1) THE CONTESTED DISTINCTION IS A MATURATION STAGE INSIDE ONE CLONAL BRANCH, NOT A BRANCH POINT. T3 asserts that a MATURE circulating CD16+ pbNK enters decidua and converts. Its live competitor after the Phase A audit is not "decidual NK are non-haematopoietic" - it is that a BLOOD-BORNE IMMATURE PRECURSOR (CD34+ or CD34-CD117+CD94- stage-3) crosses into the uterus and matures locally (Chantakru 2002 PMID 11751942; Male 2010 PMID 20802153; Vacca 2011 PMID 21248224; Strunz 2021 PMID 33617461). A mature pbNK and its sibling precursor are on the SAME clonal branch and carry the SAME mark, because the mark is fixed upstream of both. Clone membership is stage-agnostic and undirected: it says "these two cells share an ancestor", never "which one was the immigrant" or "what state it was in when it crossed the endothelium". Both hypotheses therefore predict the identical clonal structure - the prompt's own disqualifying condition. (2) THE DEPTH RESOLUTION IS WRONG BY ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE, and this is documented, not speculative. Rueckert 2022 Nat Immunol PMID 36289449, the one study that has actually run mtscATAC/mgatk on human NK cells, states in its own results that for CONVENTIONAL (non-adaptive, non-expanded) NK cells the mitochondrial mutations "do not flag clonal expansions but might instead be present already on the progenitor level". Wang 2025 Genome Biol PMID 40134031 goes further: the majority of purported clone-informative variants are PRE-EXISTING heteroplasmies present in the first cell, not de novo marks acquired during recent divisions. So the "how recently" that mtDNA delivers dates the common ancestor to an embryonic/HSC-level node, far above the pbNK-vs-precursor node T3 depends on. Every maternal haematopoietic cell in that woman - blood NK, decidual NK, decidual CD34+, and a uterus-resident precursor seeded years earlier - passes the shared-ancestor test. (3) THE ENDPOINT IS A REVERSIBLE, ENVIRONMENT-IMPOSED STATE, NOT A LINEAGE DESTINATION. "dNK-like" is operationally CD16-lo/CD9+/CD49a+/CD103+/KIR+, a TGF-beta-driven residency imprint that Keskin's own Discussion concedes "may not be specific to the decidual tissue but may occur when NK cells enter any tissue expressing TGF-beta", and that Cerdeira 2013 Fig 1 shows RUNNING BACKWARDS - ex vivo dNK lose KIR and regain cytotoxicity within 7-10 days of culture (registry claim R3 is exactly this reversal). An NK cell sitting in decidua is dNK-like whatever its recent ancestry, and an NK cell in blood is not, whatever its ancestry. Ancestry neither determines nor reports the state. NOTE ON WHAT IS DECIDABLE: a coarser question - "is the human uterine NK pool filled from the circulation at all?" - is a genuine ancestry question, but it is not T3, and it has already been answered in vivo in humans by donor/recipient genotyping rather than by barcoding (Strunz 2021 PMID 33617461, uNK carry recipient genotype after uterus transplant; Strunz 2026 Sci Transl Med PMID 41811987, donor-derived endometrial tissue-resident lymphocytes after HSCT, one case male-origin; both recorded abstract-level only in Phase A). G4 note: the structurally identical question in the T cell field - are tissue-resident cells clonally continuous with blood? - is routinely settled with TCR clonotype, a true per-cell somatic barcode with resolution mtDNA does not approach (e.g. PMID 41615802, intra-donor cross-tissue T cell clonal mapping across gut-liver-blood). NK cells have no rearranged receptor, which is precisely why the NK field is reaching for mtDNA and precisely why it cannot reach the depth this claim needs.

THE VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: you would have to determine whether the cell that crossed into the decidua was a mature CD16+ pbNK (T3 as stated) or a blood-borne CD34+/CD117+ stage-3 precursor that matured in situ. NO LINEAGE EXPERIMENT CAN DO THIS - the two candidates share a branch and share the mark - so the follow-up is not a barcoding experiment at all. b.why: The claim decomposes into three parts, and the part that carries the claim is not the part barcoding can see. (1) "Glycodelin-A DRIVES" is molecular attribution. The primitive returns whether two cells share an ancestor and how recently; it is blind to WHICH signal produced a state. A perfect clonal read showing blood NK gave rise to the CD9+CD49a+ cells would not name GdA as the cause, and a perfect clonal read showing no relationship would not exclude GdA from acting on whatever precursor does make dNK. (2) "dNK-LIKE PHENOTYPE" is a marker state, not an ancestry relation - lineage does not measure phenotype causation. (3) The one structurally clean question here - is the day-5 CD9+CD49a+ output the progeny of CD9-CD49a- day-0 cells (conversion), or the expansion of a CD9+CD49a+ fraction present at day 0 (selection)? - IS decidable in principle, and it is exactly Phase A's strongest alternative explanation. But that is a narrow within-culture ancestry question, not the claim as written, and it still cannot license the verb "drives". Decisively, this is the preregistered REVERSIBLE-STATE case. CD56bright/CD9/CD49a residency markers are a reversible state inside one NK lineage, not a lineage bifurcation: Niehrs et al. Nat Immunol 2025 (PMID 41087727) show human CD56bright NK enter tissue transiently and egress via lymphatics to recirculate, and Orrantia et al. iScience 2022 (PMID 36262311) show CD9 and the decidual-like signature are acquired by ordinary blood NK during proliferation-dominated reconstitution in vivo. So clonal sharing between the "blood NK" and "dNK-like" marker compartments is produced equally by a conversion model, by a selection-then-reversion model, and by plain recirculation - and absence of sharing is equally consistent with GdA acting on the local decidual CD34+ precursor route (Vacca et al. PNAS 2011, PMID 21248224). Both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure, which is the definition of not decidable by this primitive.

That makes A+B a single terminal timepoint per woman with no repeat sampling and no before/after GdA-exposure comparison in the same individual, which is fatal for a claim about a factor driving a transition over time. Not post-mortem-restricted. C is separately obtainable as an outpatient Pipelle endometrial biopsy in a prior cycle, so a preconception cohort could in principle assemble blood + endometrium longitudinally (cohorts of this scale exist - PMID 40561039 biopsied 924 women pre-pregnancy), but the terminal decidual sample still requires a pregnancy ending in surgery, so the full A+B+C set is only completable in women whose pregnancies are terminated or delivered surgically. D comes with B at no extra access cost. E (bone marrow) requires a separate aspirate essentially never taken alongside a termination, so an HSC-anchored version is not obtainable paired. Tooling constraint on the human arm: prospective label-based barcoding is impossible in a human pregnancy, so the only usable primitive is endogenous - mtDNA variants via mtscATAC-seq or MAESTER (PMID 35210612), or somatic epimutations (PMID 40399669) - and their clonal resolution depends on prior clonal expansion (PMID 40134031), which is precisely what is in dispute for a polyclonal blood NK pool.
b.compartment_notes: The decisive access asymmetry is species, not tissue, and it splits the claim in two so that no single organism can test it whole. PAEP/glycodelin has NO mouse or rat ortholog - the gene is lost in mouse, rat, rabbit, tarsier, megabat and dolphin and is functional only in higher primates (confirmed in Phase A). So the entire mouse lineage toolkit that could address the structural clause - T-bet fate mapping of decidual NK (PMID 41782473, 2026), circulating-NK-to-tissue-resident conversion demonstrated in skin (PMID 38157853), autocrine TGF-beta1 driving resident NK differentiation (PMID 39692745), Confetti/Polylox/CRISPR recorders - can never address the "glycodelin-A drives" clause without first humanizing PAEP. Conversely the human arm is the only place GdA exists, and there prospective barcoding is unavailable, leaving only endogenous mtDNA/epimutation readouts on surgically-constrained single-timepoint tissue. Note also that the structural question underneath this claim - do circulating cells convert to a tissue-resident state, or is the resident pool locally derived - has already been attacked with lineage tools in the adjacent fields the mechanism is borrowed from: skin NK residency (PMID 38157853), rhesus macaque NK clonal compartmentalization by lentiviral barcoding (PMID 30389798, PMID 31649681), and blood-versus-tonsil compartmentalized human T cell clones (PMID 41308653). None of these were run on decidua, and none of them could attribute the transition to a named ligand, which is the same wall this claim hits.

b.why:
FALSE — this is the reversible-state carve-out, and it fails on three independent grounds.

(1) THE PREDICATE IS A STATE, NOT AN ANCESTRY RELATION. The claim is "IL-35 drives NK TOWARD a CD9+CD103+CD49a+ ILC1-like PHENOTYPE." Both operative terms are non-lineage: "toward ... phenotype" is directional state language, and "ILC1-like" is a functional/phenotypic predicate. The primitive (do two cells share an ancestor, how recently) returns nothing about whether a cell is ILC1-like. This is the rubric's "A becomes functionally B-like" case.

(2) BOTH READINGS PRODUCE THE SAME CLONAL TOPOLOGY — the decisive point. The two live interpretations are (a) genuine differentiation of cNK into an ILC1-like cell, and (b) a reversible, cytokine-maintained surface program (three integrins/tetraspanin) layered on unchanged cNK. Under BOTH, barcodes straddle the CD49a-/CD49a+ boundary: clones appear in both marker fractions at intermediate timepoints and the whole day-0 repertoire is represented by day 8. There is no barcode topology that separates "converted" from "transiently up-regulated ITGA1/ITGAE/CD9," because no lineage branch is created in either case. Clonal structure is degenerate with respect to the question actually being asked. The 48 h washout non-reversal reported by the source does not rescue this — 48 h of marker persistence is not a heritable branch, and the cross-field literature says the program is generic and reversible over longer horizons (Fonseca ex-TRM, PMID 32066954; Zitti Immunity 2023, PMID 37269830, showing IL-15+TGF-b induces CD49a and a TRM program on CIRCULATING human CD8 T cells, RUNX2/RUNX3-dependent — i.e. the same integrin program is cross-lineage and therefore not lineage-diagnostic).

(3) THE CAUSAL CLAUSE IS OUTSIDE THE PRIMITIVE. "IL-35 drives" is a perturbation-attribution claim. Lineage supplies no causal attribution; and the proximal cause in the source's own data is autocrine TGF-b (fully abrogated by anti-TGF-b1/2/3 and Galunisertib, reproduced by TGF-b alone), so the clause is one step upstream of the measured mechanism regardless of any clonal readout.

WHAT IS DECIDABLE, AND WHY IT DOES NOT SAVE THE ROW: there is a narrow lineage-shaped residue the claim does not assert — "is the CD9+CD103+CD49a+ population the clonal progeny of marker-negative cNK, or the outgrowth of a pre-existing, clonally distinct subset?" That is a legitimate same/different-lineage question and is decidable in principle (mtDNA-variant tracking or lentiviral barcoding on day-0 blood NK, indexed on the marker triad). This is why T6 is a near-miss rather than a trivial FALSE. But it is not the claim, it fails B2 below, and it is gated on a marker definition the field itself calls unresolved: Wu et al. (PMID 36605190, PMC9808525), the only primate barcode study of blood-vs-tissue NK clonality, states outright that "definitive markers to distinguish NK from ILCs in tissues remain unresolved" and that they "are not able to exclude the presence of ILCs." A clonal answer inherits the gate it is asked to adjudicate; if "ILC1-like" is defined by the very markers in dispute, the barcode result is only as meaningful as the sort.

(Decidability here does not depend on the Phase A dispute over the primary source's verification status — the claim's structure fails the primitive either way.)

ANSWER = YES (clones straddle the boundary; barcodes/mtDNA clones found in BOTH the CD9+CD103+CD49a+ and marker-negative fractions of the same day-4 well, converted cells drawn from across the day-0 repertoire with no clonal restriction) => reading: "conversion, not selection."

VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: nothing lineage-shaped. Concretely, all three next moves are non-clonal:
(a) REAGENT QC — assay PeproTech 200-37 single-chain IL-35 (HEK293, 406-aa IL12A-EBI3 fusion, used at 100 ng/mL) against vehicle on a Ba/F3-gp130-IL-12Rb1-IL-12Rb2 reporter with pSTAT1/pSTAT4 readout, i.e. the Aparicio-Siegmund assay (PMID 25259790), because if the recombinant is inactive or carries a TGF-b-inducing contaminant the clonal result is about a different molecule entirely.
(b) IS THE STATE A SET-POINT OR AN ENDPOINT — extend washout well past 48 h (7-14 d) and add Galunisertib AFTER conversion is established, asking whether CD9/CD103/CD49a revert. A revertible marker set is a state, not a fate.
(c) IS "ILC1-LIKE" ANYTHING BEYOND GENERIC TGF-b RESIDENCY — score the same cells against a CD8 TRM program (ITGA1, ITGAE, RUNX2, CD9) alongside the paper's ILC1 UCell signature; PMID 37269830 predicts they are the same program, which would void the ILC1 interpretation without touching lineage.

None of (a)-(c) requires or uses the barcodes. The YES answer changes nothing about what you do next.
b.action_if_no:
ANSWER = NO (clones partition; the CD9+CD103+CD49a+ cells trace to a restricted set of pre-existing day-0 clones essentially absent from the marker-negative fraction) => reading: "selection/outgrowth of a pre-existing subset."

VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: first, disbelieve the assay, then run the same three experiments as the YES branch.
(a) ASSAY CONTROL FIRST — re-run the culture starting from a FACS-purified CD9-CD103-CD49a- day-0 fraction. This is the single control Phase A already flags as missing (t=0 was never gated marker-negative), it is a one-day flow experiment, and it settles selection-vs-conversion completely WITHOUT any barcodes. A NO result would also be immediately suspect on technical grounds: lentiviral barcoding requires activation/transduction that itself induces CD103/CD49a through the same TGF-b axis being studied, and an <=8-day culture in which IL-35 SUPPRESSES proliferation gives mtDNA-based tracking almost no dividing generations, so apparent clonal partition is confounded by near-zero clonal resolution. The first response to NO is therefore to re-test the instrument, not to act on the biology.
(b) then the identical REAGENT QC (PMID 25259790 assay), and
(c) then the identical TGF-b-dependence / TRM-vs-ILC1 signature-specificity tests.

So even the "interesting" branch routes through a cheap flow control that makes the lineage assay redundant, and then converges on the YES branch's experiments.
b.both_answers_reason:
FALSE — fails on all three of the strict tests: convergence, vacuity, and wrong-instrument.

CONVERGENCE. After stripping the assay-control step, the YES and NO branches terminate in the SAME two experiments: (i) validate the single-chain IL-35 reagent on an IL-35R reporter, and (ii) determine whether the CD9/CD103/CD49a program is a TGF-b-maintained reversible set-point and whether it is distinguishable from the generic CD8 TRM program. The load-bearing uncertainties in this claim — reagent validity, mechanistic displacement onto TGF-b, and whether "ILC1-like" is a real identity or a generic integrin signature — are all non-lineage, so the clonal answer does not gate any of them. Whichever way the barcodes fall, the next bench day is identical.

VACUITY OF THE YES BRANCH. YES is not a discriminating outcome, it is the answer already forced by data in hand: IL-35 suppresses proliferation, survival is unchanged out to day 9, "nearly all cells" are marker-positive by day 8 (arithmetically unreachable by selecting a near-absent blood precursor in the absence of division), and both >98%-pure sorted NKG2C+ and >98%-pure sorted NKG2C- subsets converted independently. A prospective clonal assay whose result is pre-determined by existing controls returns "conversion confirmed, proceed to the experiments we already needed" — the textbook vacuous branch.

WRONG INSTRUMENT FOR THE ONLY DECIDABLE RESIDUE. The one sub-question lineage could answer (pre-existing subset vs conversion) is answered more cheaply, more directly, and without the transduction/proliferation confounds by a single FACS step: purify CD9-CD103-CD49a- NK at t=0 and re-run. Since that control is a mandatory prerequisite in BOTH branches anyway, the clonal experiment is dominated by a control that must be run regardless. Spending a barcoding assay to reach a conclusion that a one-day sort already delivers is not an actionable fork.

RESIDUAL ASYMMETRY, AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH. A strict steelman: NO would overturn the source's central claim and its downstream pan-cancer/TCGA inference, and would prompt prospective isolation of a distinct CD9+CD103+CD49a+ blood precursor — nominally a different experiment from the YES branch. But (1) NO is close to excluded a priori by the proliferation/survival/sorted-subset data above, (2) the first and correct response to NO is to suspect the assay's own artifacts rather than the biology, and (3) prospective isolation of that precursor is again the same t=0 sort. The asymmetry is nominal, not operational. OUT.
b.compartments_needed:
Two distinct compartment sets, depending on which version of the claim is adjudicated.

VERSION 1 — the in vitro claim as actually evidenced (population-frequency shift in culture):
  A. Day-0 human peripheral blood CD56+CD3- NK, prospectively gated CD9-CD103-CD49a- (the marker-negative starting compartment).
  B. Day-4 and day-8 CD9+CD103+CD49a+ cells from the IL-35 arm of the SAME well.
  B'. Day-4/day-8 marker-NEGATIVE cells from that same well (the within-well comparator that makes the straddle-vs-partition read possible; without it there is no boundary to test).
  C. The paired IL-2-alone well from the SAME donor.
All four come from one buffy coat or leukapheresis from one healthy donor, split across wells. Same individual by construction.

VERSION 2 — the in vivo claim the result is deployed to support (tumour NK are IL-35-converted ILC1-like cells):
  A. Autologous peripheral blood cNK from the patient.
  B. Tumour-infiltrating CD9+CD103+CD49a+ group-1 ILC from the resected lesion.
  C. Adjacent non-malignant tissue from the same organ (to separate tumour-driven from tissue-intrinsic residency).
  D. A compartment defined by prior IL-35 EXPOSURE — required for the "IL-35 drives" clause, and it does not exist as a sortable population.

OPTIONAL PHYSIOLOGICAL COMPARATOR (if one wants the natural human CD9+CD49a+ compartment rather than tumour): decidual NK, for which CD9+CD49a+ is the canonical hallmark; or liver-resident CD49a+ NK.
b.compartments_obtainable:
MIXED — TRUE and trivially so for Version 1; TRUE-but-surgical for the tissue arm of Version 2; STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for the compartment that carries the claim's causal clause.

VERSION 1: FULLY OBTAINABLE, PAIRED, FROM ONE HUMAN, WITH NO ANATOMICAL OR ETHICAL CONSTRAINT. A single healthy-donor buffy coat split across wells yields A, B, B' and C simultaneously from the same individual. Not post-mortem, not surgical, not pregnancy-limited, not mouse-only. This is one of the rare rows where compartment access is a complete non-issue — which is precisely why T6 must be killed on B1/B2 rather than on B3. Compartment availability is not the binding constraint here.

VERSION 2: A is a routine blood draw (obtainable paired at induction of anaesthesia). B and C are SURGERY-ONLY — they require a resection specimen or biopsy; there is no non-surgical route to tumour-infiltrating or adjacent-normal lymphocytes. Paired blood+tumour+adjacent-normal from one patient is nonetheless standard practice in tumour immunology and is exactly the sampling underlying the public cohorts (lung, oesophagus, colon, breast) that the source re-analysed in silico rather than sampling itself. So B/C are obtainable, at surgery, paired, from one human.

COMPARTMENT D IS NOT OBTAINABLE IN ANY SPECIES-APPROPRIATE FORM. Prior IL-35 exposure is not a sortable cell property, there is no fate-mark for having seen IL-35, and no human in vivo IL-35 perturbation exists. A tumour cell that converted in vivo carries no feature distinguishing it from a tissue ILC1 of separate ontogeny. This — not tissue access — is the real compartment failure, and no amount of specimen collection fixes it.

OPTIONAL COMPARATORS, flagged explicitly as the brief requires: decidual NK (the canonical human CD9+CD49a+ compartment) is PREGNANCY-ONLY, obtainable solely at elective termination or delivery, and can never be paired with the same individual's pre-conversion state under a controlled perturbation. Liver-resident CD49a+ NK are TRANSPLANT/PERFUSATE- or POST-MORTEM-ONLY in humans.
b.compartment_notes:
SPECIES SCISSORS — the structurally important note. The compartments are obtainable in the species where the perturbation cannot be performed (human: blood and tumour are easy, but no in vivo IL-35 challenge and no fate-mark), while the perturbation-plus-fate-map version is only executable in the species where the claim was never made (mouse: Ebi3/Il12a conditional deletion, Ncr1/Eomes fate maps, parabiosis, Polylox/confetti). Human IL-35 reagent biology and the human CD9/CD103/CD49a triad do not transfer cleanly to mouse, and the mouse literature already routes this phenotype through TGF-b rather than IL-35. So the two halves of a decisive experiment sit in different organisms and cannot be joined.

NEAREST EXISTING OCCUPANCY FOUND (informational, for the shortlist's benefit; not a formal B4 verdict): Wu et al., Front Immunol 2022, PMID 36605190 / PMC9808525, archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/T6_PMC9808525.txt — autologous barcoded-HSPC transplant in rhesus macaque tracking clonal relationships of NK across peripheral blood, liver, spleen, lung and GI tract. This is the closest thing to the structural question ("are marker-defined tissue NK clonally the same population as blood NK?") actually executed with a clonal primitive in a primate, and it reports tissue-restricted NK clone sets alongside shared blood/tissue clones. It also supplies the caveat that guts the marker gate: "definitive markers to distinguish NK from ILCs in tissues remain unresolved," authors "not able to exclude the presence of ILCs." Also found: PMID 40621477 (lentiviral barcode delivery into human and rhesus NK — establishes the barcoding is technically feasible in NK, which is why B2 rather than feasibility is the binding failure).

SEARCH HONESTY (rule G3): my targeted searches for mtDNA/mtscATAC/MAESTER applied specifically to NK or ILC1, and for Polylox/CRISPR-recorder/confetti applied to NK-to-ILC1 conversion, returned reviews and off-target hits only — thin and ambiguous. I am NOT recording those as "nobody has done it." Treat the already_traced status for the mtDNA-in-NK and recorder-in-ILC1 arms as NOT_SEARCHED, not FALSE. The Phase A adversarial pass separately documents the relevant in vivo primary sources (Flommersfeld PMID 34437840 single-cell colour-barcoding + parabiosis; Gao PMID 28759001; Cortez PMID 27156386; Sojka PMID 24714492; Gasteiger PMID 26472762), and per G4 the T cell/TRM field has already answered the same structural question by TCR clonal-repertoire overlap between paired blood and skin (Zitti, PMID 37269830) — the clonal step NK cells cannot borrow, having no rearranged receptor.

BOTTOM LINE FOR THE SHORTLIST: T6 is OUT, failing B1 (cytokine-induced reversible within-lineage state; both readings share one clonal topology) and failing B2 decisively (convergent branches, vacuous YES, and a one-day FACS control that dominates the lineage assay). b.why:
DECIDABLE, but only in a specific reading, and two of the claim's three clauses have to be handled separately.

The claim bundles (a) a PROVENANCE assertion — intratumoural NK descend from the NK pool that was in that organ, not from the circulating pool; (b) a TEMPORAL assertion — that ancestral pool was in the organ before the tumour; (c) a FUNCTIONAL rider — "functional" intratumoural NK.

(a) is squarely the primitive's form ("the progeny of A are B" / "A and B are same-or-different lineage") and is DECIDABLE. The two competing hypotheses predict genuinely different clonal structures, not the same one: under X1, tumour NK coalesce recently with uninvolved-same-organ NK and only deeply (at the HSPC root) with blood NK; under the recruitment alternative (Torcellan 2024 PMID 38157853; Horowitz 2026 PMID 42090477) the reverse. The primitive's "how recently" term is what does the work — it separates "kin because both were seeded from the same marrow clone" from "kin because one locally divided into the other." This requires three compartments, not two; with only tumour+organ the answer is symmetric (organ->tumour, tumour->organ, blood->both are all consistent with the same sharing) and would fail.

(c) is NOT lineage-decidable and must be discharged by construction, not by inference: "functional" has to become a sort gate on compartment B (GzmB+/degranulating/IFN-g+ intratumoural NK) so that lineage is asked about an already-functionally-defined bucket. Lineage must never be used to argue the cells are functional.

(b) is decidable ONLY if the mark is applied before the tumour exists (photoconversion/inducible fate map/parabiosis at t0), which makes it a true lineage question — "do these tumour cells descend from the cells I marked in the organ." Read from a single post-tumour timepoint it is not a lineage property at all and must be imported as an assumption.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE REVERSIBLE-STATE TRAP, and the condition under which it becomes one. Tissue residency IS a reversible/inducible state — Torcellan 2024 shows circulating NK acquire it, Horowitz 2026 shows TGF-beta is sufficient ex vivo, Blood 2025 (PMID 40857665) shows chronic activation installs a residency-like state via KLF2 loss. If X1 were phrased as "NK acquire residency inside tumours," both answers would be consistent with one clonal structure and it would be NOT DECIDABLE. But X1 is phrased as an origin claim: which pool did these cells come from. Provenance of a cell from compartment A versus compartment B is pedigree, not state. The state is the confound here, not the claim. CONDITION: this only holds if compartments A and B are defined SPATIALLY (cells physically in the uninvolved organ vs physically in the tumour, with i.v. anti-CD45 labelling to exclude vascular contamination). If compartment A is instead defined phenotypically as CD49a+CD103+CD69+ "trNK", the compartment is a reversible state, cells enter and leave it with no lineage event, and the claim collapses back into the undecidable form. The registry must fix the spatial definition or this row is not decidable.

SECOND CONDITION, from the registry's own ontology. Because this registry treats ILC1 as distinct from NK (T4, P3), a positive result is only about X1 if the marked cells are NK-lineage — otherwise it is Dadi 2016 (PMID 26806130) again, whose resident population is Nfil3-independent and transcriptionally "distinct from conventional NK cells," and whose cNK showed HIGH non-host chimerism. Usefully, that fork is itself a lineage question the same primitive answers (do the tissue cells coalesce with blood cNK, or with an ILC-progenitor-derived clade — cf. Nixon 2022 PMID 35394814, "did not interconvert with NK cells"), so it can be settled inside the same experiment rather than assumed.
b.action_if_yes:
YES = tumour NK coalesce recently with uninvolved-organ NK and only at HSPC depth with blood NK; the pre-tumour organ label is recovered inside the established tumour.

VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: convert the pre-tumour lineage label into a functional handle and selectively ablate ONLY the resident-derived pool, before tumour induction, in the autochthonous model. Concretely: pre-tumour photoconversion or inducible Ncr1/Hobit-driven marking of the uninvolved organ in an animal carrying an inducible DTR restricted to the marked cells; deplete the marked resident pool at t0; read tumour incidence and growth against (i) unlabelled controls and (ii) a recruitment-blocked arm (S1PR/chemokine-axis blockade) that leaves the resident pool intact. This is the experiment the field currently states it cannot do — "the current lack of experimental tools to block recruitment of circulating NK cells or to specifically target the newly identified resident cells currently precludes testing this possibility" — and a YES is exactly what licenses building the tool.

WHY IT IS NOT VACUOUS: a YES makes the resident pool the causally load-bearing compartment and selects a specific therapeutic lever — preserve/expand the resident pool, i.e. the IL-15 axis chosen on residency grounds (Nixon 2022 PMID 35394814, with a filed MSKCC patent on targeting ILC1 IL-15 signalling; supported by Dadi's Il15-/- acceleration versus Nfil3-/- no-effect). It also re-reads the CD49a+ NK prognostic literature in HCC (PMID 31311791) as a genuine residency pedigree rather than a TME-exposure readout. Second, cheaper follow-on available immediately from the same clonal data: test at clone resolution whether the intratumoural clones are the same clones that were locally proliferating pre-tumour — i.e. put Dadi's EdU inference (local proliferation, not immigration) on a clonal footing.
b.action_if_no:
NO = tumour NK coalesce with blood NK and are no more related to uninvolved-organ NK than the HSPC-root baseline; the pre-tumour organ label is absent or negligible inside the tumour.

VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: a different design on a different compartment — label the CIRCULATING pool at defined times relative to tumour onset (serial photoconversion of blood/spleen, or HSPC barcoding with staggered induction) and measure (i) entry timing and dwell time of intratumoural NK, and (ii) whether a SINGLE recruited clone gives rise to both CD49a+CD103+ "trNK-like" and conventional intratumoural progeny. Point (ii) is the decisive one and is not asked at all on the YES branch: it distinguishes in-situ diversification from one entrant versus separate entrants with pre-set fates, which is precisely the Flommersfeld 2021 (PMID 34437840) selection-versus-conversion fork that those authors named for tumours themselves. The macrophage field has already run this exact design with photoconversion (PMID 40523200: dwell-time-dependent divergence of monocyte-derived TAM fates), so the protocol is off the shelf.

WHY IT IS NOT VACUOUS: a NO flips the therapeutic lever from preserve-the-resident-pool to promote-recruitment-then-impose-residency, which is the Horowitz ex-vivo TGF-beta ctrNK manufacturing route (PMID 42090477) — and a NO would establish that the manufactured product recapitulates a real in vivo route rather than a flask artefact, which is currently unknown. It also inverts the causal reading of the CD49a+ HCC prognostic signal (pedigree -> TME-exposure biomarker), and it demotes the IL-15/resident axis as a mis-chosen lever. Within this registry it hands the phenomenon to T1 (cNK -> trNK) with a specific, differently designed test rather than terminating inquiry.

TRUE, but bound to the mouse pre-tumour-label design; the human-only version FAILS this filter and I record that separately below.
